title: Grateful Dead Live at Family Dog at the Great Highway on 1969-11-02
venue: Family Dog at the Great Highway
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> SEK'D Prodif Plus -> Samplitude v8.01 Professional -> FLAC
source: Disc 1: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat (44.1k) DDisc 2: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat (44.1k) D

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard recording with crystal‑clear mix (aside from brief digital glitches) capturing a monster 1969 show highlighted by a soaring Dark Star and powerhouse Death Don't Have No Mercy.
ai_review.review: The November 2, 1969 Family Dog performance is hailed as one of the band’s late‑’69 peaks – a 48‑minute Dark Star, fiery St. Stephen → The Eleven → Death Don’t Have No Mercy and an unforgettable Jerry scream.  Charlie Miller’s soundboard transfer is generally praised for its depth and clarity, though several reviewers note brief digital noise in the middle of Dark Star.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high praise for both musical performance (standout jams, energy) and recording quality, with only minor technical complaints that do not detract from overall enjoyment.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, deep mix with excellent bass clarity; a few seconds of digital noise/distortion in Dark Star (5:16‑5:23 and ~5:57) are noted but do not overwhelm the listening experience.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The show opens with heavy psychedelic jams (Cold Rain, Dark Star) then moves into folk‑rock territory before closing on high‑energy rockers; three consecutive Pigpen numbers are a unique highlight.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar tone is praised as perfect and his iconic scream at the end of St. Stephen is singled out as a favorite moment.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil Lesh’s bass is described as ‘beyond amazing,’ deep, clear and booming throughout the set.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s country‑flavored rendition of Seasons of My Heart showcases his strong craftsmanship on early‑’70 material.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten’s keyboard work adds a richer, more expansive texture to the performance, freeing Pigpen for percussion.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann and Mickey Hart provide a solid rhythmic foundation, with Mickey’s addition noted as adding another layer of depth.
